problemStatement.formal: (a) Is there a K4-free graph whose every countable edge-coloring has a monochromatic triangle? (b) Is there a graph with no K_aleph1 whose every countable edge-coloring has a monochromatic K_aleph0?
problemStatement.plain: Can highly clique-restricted graphs still force monochromatic cliques under countably many edge colors?
whyMatters: This is an Erdos-Hajnal Ramsey question at the boundary between graph structure and set theory.
The finite and infinite parts ask how much clique-freeness is compatible with countable-color Ramsey behavior.
The Lean file currently supplies clean definitions and a sanity-check theorem rather than deep consistency machinery.

The statements `erdos_1174a` and `erdos_1174b` formalize the two existence questions.
Lean proves `complete_graph_not_k4free`, showing the complete graph is excluded by the finite constraint.
